#!/usr/bin/env bash
# translate_one_application.sh — TRANSLATE_ONE_APPLICATION.md as a runnable loop.
#
# Grows the translation pipeline for ONE app: mine the app's construct
# footprint -> emit minimal probe templates -> run the oracle (source-native
# vs target) -> drive pi (default model deepseek-v4-turbo) to fix red probes
# -> gate (ladder + acceptance tests). Implements the playbook's discipline:
# one construct per probe, refuse > guess, no-regression guard, escalate via
# core-requests, never `git add .`.
#
# Usage:
#   ./translate_one_application.sh mine  <app> [--lang L] [--work DIR]
#   ./translate_one_application.sh probe  [--lang L] [--work DIR]
#   ./translate_one_application.sh fix    [--lang L] [--work DIR] [--commit]
#   ./translate_one_application.sh gate   [--lang L] [--work DIR] [--tests DIR]
#   ./translate_one_application.sh run    <app> [--lang L] [--target estree|perl|c|sh]
#                                        [--tests DIR] [--iterations N] [--commit]
#   ./translate_one_application.sh dump-templates --lang L
#
# Language: detected from the app extension (sh|zsh|fish|py|pl|go) or --lang.
#   c   -> cc + frontends/c-sh-go        (C subset)
#   sh  -> bash + frontends/posix-sh-go  (byte-equality oracle)
#   zsh -> zsh  + frontends/zsh-sh-go    (byte-eq with the subscript waiver)
#   fish-> fish + frontends/fish-sh-go
#   py  -> python3 + frontends/py-sh-go
#   pl  -> perl + frontends/perl-sh-go
#   go  -> go (wrapper) + frontends/go-sh
# Target (default estree): estree | perl | c | sh | rust  (estree executes
# end-to-end via the sh2 runner; rust renders + rustc-compiles + runs; the
# rest render only).
#
# Environment: MODEL (pi model, default deepseek-v4-turbo), THINKING,
# WORK (.translate-work), TPLDIR (templates/), MAX_ATTEMPTS (3),
# MAX_PROBES (16), TIMEOUT (20), COMMIT (0/1).
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SUB="$ROOT/sh2perl"

The corpus is green (103/103). The dog-food app integration is the real remaining task. The only blocker is `shiremit.Emit`. This is a well-defined, focused change.

Given the complexity, my approach: the frontend already has a `json.Marshal(x)` -> `jsonMarshal` call lowering precedent. The cleanest way to make `go-sh.go` self-host is to lower `shiremit.Emit(prog)` to an A1 node that, at runtime, re-serializes the parsed program.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fail-go-app — the go-sh DOGFOOD app gate: the go frontend transpiles
# ITSELF (cmd/go-sh/main.go + go-sh.go + shir-emit-go/emit.go — the
# concatenated package the CLI's PACKAGE MODE sees) into JS, and the JS
# CLI must produce the SAME A1 JSON as the native go-sh binary.
#
#   oracle: frontends/go-sh/go-sh --shir <input.go> --raw   (the original)
#   js    : <concat> --shir → debashc --shir-in-estree → estree-runner.mjs
#           run with --args --shir <input.go> --raw
#
# A test passes only on oracle == js stdout (byte-for-byte). The corpus
# inputs are frontends/go-sh/testdata/*.go (the same ladder the corpus
# gate uses).
#
# Usage: ./fail-go-app [--gate] [PREFIX]
set -u
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
GOSH="$ROOT/frontends/go-sh/go-sh"
DEBASHC="$ROOT/sh2perl/target/debug/debashc"
RUNNER="$ROOT/harness/estree-runner.mjs"
CONCAT="$ROOT/frontends/go-sh/cmd/go-sh/main.go $ROOT/frontends/go-sh/go-sh.go $ROOT/frontends/shir-emit-go/emit.go"
CORPUS="$ROOT/frontends/go-sh/testdata"
TIMEOUT=180
GATE=0; PREFIX=""
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --gate) GATE=1 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,20p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) [ -z "$PREFIX" ] && PREFIX="$a" ;;
  esac
done

[ -x "$DEBASHC" ] || { echo "oracle debashc missing" >&2; exit 1; }

tmpd=$(mktemp -d)
cat $CONCAT > "$tmpd/app.go"
# transpile the app ONCE (the same A1/estree for every input)
if ! timeout 120 "$GOSH" --shir "$tmpd/app.go" --raw > "$tmpd/app.a1.json" 2>"$tmpd/a1.err"; then
  echo "FAIL: the go frontend cannot parse its own sources:" >&2
  head -3 "$tmpd/a1.err" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! timeout 180 "$DEBASHC" --shir-in-estree - < "$tmpd/app.a1.json" > "$tmpd/app.estree.json" 2>"$tmpd/estree.err"; then
  echo "FAIL: the app's A1 is rejected by the estree ingress:" >&2
  head -3 "$tmpd/estree.err" >&2
  exit 1
fi

pass=0; fail=0; total=0
for f in "$CORPUS"/*.go; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  bn=$(basename "$f")
  [ -n "$PREFIX" ] && [[ "$bn" == "$PREFIX"* ]] || [ -z "$PREFIX" ] || continue
  total=$((total+1))
  # oracle: the native go-sh binary
  oracle=$(timeout 60 "$GOSH" --shir "$f" --raw 2>/dev/null)
  # js: the transpiled CLI run with the same args
  js=$(timeout "$TIMEOUT" node "$RUNNER" "$tmpd/app.estree.json" --source "$tmpd/app.go" \
       --args --shir "$f" --raw 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$oracle" = "$js" ]; then
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    fail=$((fail+1))
    echo "  $bn MISMATCH (oracle ${#oracle}B vs js ${#js}B)"
  fi
done
echo "=== fail-go-app: $pass/$total js pass (the go frontend transpiles itself) ==="
rm -rf "$tmpd"
[ "$GATE" = 1 ] && [ "$fail" -gt 0 ] && exit 1
exit 0
=====FAIL-GO=====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fail-go — Go→JS / Go→Rust end-to-end gate (TRANSLATE_ONE_APPLICATION dog-food).
#
# For every Go source file (default: frontends/go-sh/testdata/*.go — the
# frontend's corpus ladder), the oracle is the SOURCE's native behavior
# (`go run` of the program; snippets are wrapped with package main + a
# detected-imports stub, mirroring translate_one_application.sh run_native):
#
#   JS  : go-sh --shir --raw → debashc --shir-in-estree → estree-runner.mjs
#   Rust: go-sh --shir --raw → otranspilerl --target rust → rustc → run
#
# A test passes only on its own verdict (oracle == translated stdout),
# never by render success alone. No failing-test allowlist: a red probe is
# the pipeline's gap signal (the TRANSLATE_ONE_APPLICATION fix loop).
#
# FLAKINESS GUARD (re-verification, NOT an allowlist): a single transient
# infra failure — a `go run` oracle that dies (rc=124 timeout / compile
# hiccup), an estree-runner node killed or returning empty under load, or
# the shared target dir's debashc being churned by another worker — can
# false-red one test as js=MISMATCH (e.g. the 18:47:06 t16-t19 flake,
# green 17s later and in 39 consecutive runs). one() re-runs the whole
# per-test measurement ONCE before trusting a non-PASS verdict (the same
# re-check the operator does by hand), and the second attempt's verdict is
# final — a real transpiler bug reproduces on retry and still counts as a
# failure. Deterministic frontend rejections (EMIT-FAIL / REFUSE) are not
# retried. The per-test oracle rc is surfaced in the summary for
# diagnosis, so a recurring infra flake stays visible.
#
# Usage: ./fail-go [--gate] [--rust] [--app FILE.go] [PREFIX]
#   default    report per-file {file, oracle, js, rust, reason}
#   --gate     exit 1 on any failure (js unless --rust; both with --rust)
#   --rust     also (or only) run the rust target
#   --app FILE run a single app (the dog-food integration test) + the corpus
#   PREFIX     filename prefix filter (like ./fail)
set -u

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
GOSH="$ROOT/frontends/go-sh/go-sh"
DEBASHC="$ROOT/sh2perl/target/debug/debashc"
OTRANS="$ROOT/otranspilerl/target/debug/otranspilerl-cli"
# the rust BACKEND renderer — the worktree's debashc --shir-in-rust
# (harness/triage.sh + harness/repro-pair.sh use the same binary). The
# otranspilerl-cli fallback links the MAIN checkout's stale renderer
# copy — used only when the worktree binary isn't built (standalone
# runs outside the backend gate, which builds it first).
RUSTBIN="$ROOT/sh2perl/backends/rust/target/debug/debashc"
[ -x "$RUSTBIN" ] || RUSTBIN="$OTRANS"
RUNNER="$ROOT/harness/estree-runner.mjs"
CORPUS="$ROOT/frontends/go-sh/testdata"
TIMEOUT=15
JOBS="$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 4)"

GATE=0; RUST=0; APP=""; PREFIX=""
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --gate) GATE=1 ;;
    --rust) RUST=1 ;;
    --app) APP="${2:-}" ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,20p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) [ -z "$PREFIX" ] && PREFIX="$a" ;;
  esac
done
[ -n "$APP" ] && shift 2

# ── A1-ingress oracle ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The main checkout's target dir is SHARED with the core/estree/sh
# workers (build-lock.sh default), and they churn or wipe it (cargo
# clean, rebuilds, lockfile revert/stale serde caches) — the binary can
# vanish between `make test`'s debashc-oracle check and this script's
# run. A missing oracle must report "oracle unavailable", never a
# misleading "A1->estree failed" (rc=127 masquerades as a renderer
# rejection). Rebuild through the sanctioned choke point (backend role:
# waits up to 1800s, never preempts) — same as make debashc-oracle,
# including the documented stale-cache retry (serde 1.0.229 artifacts
# vs a reverted 1.0.226 lockfile; cleaning just those packages recovers
# without nuking the shared dep cache).
ensure_oracle() {
  [ -x "$DEBASHC" ] && return 0
  echo "oracle $(basename "$DEBASHC") missing — rebuilding via build-lock.sh" >&2
  if "$ROOT/harness/build-lock.sh" --role backend -- cargo build \
      --manifest-path "$ROOT/sh2perl/Cargo.toml" --bin debashc >&2; then
    echo "oracle rebuilt" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  echo "oracle build failed — stale serde cache? cleaning serde artifacts and retrying once" >&2
  if "$ROOT/harness/build-lock.sh" --role backend -- cargo clean \
        --manifest-path "$ROOT/sh2perl/Cargo.toml" -p serde_derive -p serde -p serde_core >&2 \
      && "$ROOT/harness/build-lock.sh" --role backend -- cargo build \
        --manifest-path "$ROOT/sh2perl/Cargo.toml" --bin debashc >&2; then
    echo "oracle rebuilt after serde cache clean" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  echo "FAIL (oracle unavailable — could not build debashc; the core tree may be mid-WIP)" >&2
  return 1
}
ensure_oracle || exit 1

# ── helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
wrap_go() { # file -> wrapped program on stdout (if it needs wrapping)
  local f="$1" imports=""
  grep -q 'func main(' "$f" && { cat "$f"; return; }
  grep -q 'fmt\.'       "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"fmt\""
  grep -q 'strings\.'   "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"strings\""
  grep -q 'bufio\.'     "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"bufio\""
  grep -qE 'os\.(Getenv|WriteFile|Setenv|Stat|Stdin|Stdout|Stderr|ReadFile|Args)' "$f" \
    && imports="$imports\n\t\"os\""
  grep -q 'exec\.'      "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"os/exec\""
  grep -q 'strconv\.'   "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"strconv\""
  grep -q 'filepath\.'  "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"path/filepath\""
  grep -q 'bytes\.'     "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"bytes\""
  grep -q 'sort\.'      "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"sort\""
  grep -q 'time\.'      "$f" && imports="$imports\n\t\"time\""
  { printf 'package main\n\nimport (\n%b\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n' "$imports"; cat "$f"; printf '\n}\n'; }
}

measure_once() { # f -> run oracle+JS(+Rust) ONCE; store MO MORC MJ MJRC MJv MR MRRC MRv MREASON
  local f="$1" wrp tmp o orc a1 jrc e rs rsrc reason="" R= J= rc
  wrp=$(wrap_go "$f")
  tmp=$(mktemp -d)
  printf '%s\n' "$wrp" > "$tmp/main.go"
